title: Granny stripe panel
subtitle: Continuous granny-style rows worked back and forth to build a striped panel without joining separate motifs
excerpt: The granny stripe panel works the cluster-and-chain construction of the granny square continuously back and forth across a row rather than in separate joined squares. Each cluster row produces a stripe, and the turning gives the clusters a chevron offset between rows. No motifs to join — just rows of clusters in sequence.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1887), continuous cluster stripe chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A granny stripe crochet panel in alternating sage, cream, and terracotta DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Cluster rows in horizontal stripes, 20 cm wide panel visible.

crochet.gaugeText: Panel gauge: 3 cluster groups (9 tr) = 10 cm, 4 rows = 10 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Variable. Foundation chain sets the width; each stripe row adds 3 cm to the length.

chartDefinition.title: Granny stripe panel
chartDefinition.caption: Cluster rows worked continuously back and forth. Each row: 3tr cluster, ch 1 repeat. Colours change every row for a stripe sequence.

glossaryTerms.definition: A row of evenly spaced treble-cluster groups separated by chain-1 spaces, worked continuously across the full width of the panel without joins. Changes colour at the end of each row for the stripe effect.

content.text: The granny stripe panel takes the

of a granny square and extends it across the full panel width. Turning at each end gives the clusters a half-group offset between rows, producing a brick-pattern alignment of clusters rather than straight vertical columns.
Change colour at the end of every row to produce a horizontal stripe. Carry the unused colours up the side edge for a two or three-colour stripe sequence without cutting and rejoining every row.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: DK-weight cotton in two or three colours. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle.

content.text: Ch 34 in colour A. (For a wider panel: foundation chain = number of cluster groups × 3 + 4.)
3 tr into 4th ch from hook. *Ch 1. Skip 2 ch. 3 tr into next ch.* Rep across. Turn. (10 cluster groups.)
Ch 3. Skip first cluster. 3 tr into first ch-1 sp. *Ch 1. 3 tr into next ch-1 sp.* Rep across. 1 tr into top of turning ch. Turn.

Continue in stripe sequence, alternating colours every row. Rows 1, 3, 5 work into the foundation and odd-row ch-1 sps. Rows 2, 4, 6 work into the even-row ch-1 sps. The alternating start position produces the brick offset automatically.
Work the circular base motif for a different construction that uses the same cluster structure but in the round to produce a circle rather than a panel.
